rubric_items.reason: All 7 acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-14; the story's no-show goal and the design choice are under Out of scope with reasons.
REQs are split per count and per Last visit part and are checkable; REQ-1 leaves open whether the literal 'Visit summary' label is rendered.
Every REQ cites the ticket line; REQ-7, REQ-8, REQ-9 also cite the user's IDE answers A-01..A-03, which match what the artifact says. Nothing invented.
No clash with baseline goals, constraints, closed-appointment or data-protection rules; the ticket-vs-code date format gap was asked (Q-01) and its mismatch recorded.
Three precise questions with real options, each answered in the IDE; none remain open or block needlessly.
Plain wording; Completed, No-show, Cancelled, Scheduled and Medical history used as in the glossary.

findings.text: The Out-of-scope design note states the patient page's appointment list is loaded with a row limit, but cites no product code line for this fact.

cites.quote: the patient page's appointment list is loaded with a row limit

findings.suggested_fix: Add a cite to the repository method that limits the patient's appointments, so design can verify the REQ-6 risk.

findings.text: REQ-1 does not say whether the text 'Visit summary' is itself displayed as a label or only names the line, so a tester cannot check it unambiguously.

cites.quote: a `Visit summary` line is shown directly above the Appointments table.

findings.suggested_fix: State whether a 'Visit summary' label or heading is rendered, or that the name only identifies the line.
